findings.body:
**Implement the required machine-mode contract.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/prepare-host.py:805`, an invocation with `--json` fails because the parser does not define that option. Operational errors at Line 839 also leave stdout empty. Success always writes narration to stderr.

Add `--json`, emit the required JSON error object, preserve the specified exit codes, and suppress stderr in machine mode.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires “stdout is JSON, stderr is narration” and “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Implement the required machine-mode contract.

findings.body:
**Reject tracked runner changes before preparing units.**

`prepare` validates the tag and commit, but it never checks the working tree. A modified runtime file in the checkout can still run after preparation succeeds. The approved tag does not identify that code.

`prepare` calls `verify_target` at `apps/crq-python/ops/prepare-host.py:694`. `verify_target` reads only tag and commit objects. `prepare` then renders and publishes the units without a `git status` check. `switch` rejects tracked changes, so `prepare` does not apply the same guard.

The generated units run the working-tree code. `crq-tick.service` sets `WorkingDirectory=@CRQ_ROOT@` and `ExecStart=/usr/bin/env python3 @CRQ_ROOT@/crq.py tick`. No startup check verifies the executed files.

Under `tick_lock`, before the units are published, reject tracked changes to runtime code. Use the same status check as `switch`, and exclude the rendered config file that `prepare` writes.
findings.title: Reject tracked runner changes before preparing units.

findings.body:
**Reject shared drop-ins that apply to the selected units.**

Systemd also applies dash-prefix drop-ins such as `crq-.service.d/` and type-wide drop-ins such as `service.d/`. These directories can change the selected service’s effective configuration. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/249/systemd.unit.html?utm_source=openai))

`unit-live-binding.py:563` rejects only exact-unit drop-in directories. Both shared directory names also evade the prefix check at Line 556. If their `.conf` files contain only service settings, the dependency scan adds no warning and discovery returns `supported=True`. Reject all applicable shared drop-ins before certifying the topology.
findings.title: Reject shared drop-ins that apply to the selected units.

findings.body:
**Emit a JSON artifact when a health observation raises.**

If `state/runs` exists but cannot be listed, `run_metadata_sample` raises `OSError`. `deploy-controller.py:2144` rethrows that error. The module-level handler then exits with plain text and leaves stdout empty. Emit an error artifact here and retain exit code 1.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires: “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout.”
findings.title: Emit a JSON artifact when a health observation raises.

findings.body:
**Join continued dependency lines before scanning them.**

Systemd joins lines that end with a backslash. Thus, `Wants=\` followed by an indented `crq-tick.service` declares a dependency. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/248/systemd.syntax.html?utm_source=openai))

At `unit-live-binding.py:460`, neither physical line produces that dependency: the first has no unit name, and the second has no directive. An otherwise ordinary `other.service` can therefore reference the selected CRQ service while discovery returns `supported=True`. This defeats the declared foreign-dependency check. Join logical lines before matching, or refuse continuation syntax.
findings.title: Join continued dependency lines before scanning them.

findings.body:
**Reject non-object dependency metadata with `ArtifactError`.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/package-runner.py:169`, a dependency `package.json` containing `[]` or `null` raises `AttributeError`. The CLI exception handler does not catch this exception. With `--json`, the command writes a traceback to stderr and produces no JSON artifact.

Check that `document` is a dictionary before calling `.get()`.

As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty” and an error without a result must produce one JSON error object.
findings.title: Reject non-object dependency metadata with `ArtifactError`.

findings.body:
**Resolve relative `--node` paths before changing `cwd`.**

At `apps/crq-python/ops/package-runner.py:560`, `--node ./node24/bin/node` is resolved relative to the extracted archive because the subprocess uses `cwd=root`. An executable that exists relative to the invocation directory therefore fails with `FileNotFoundError`. `smoke_runner` has the same problem at Line 584.

Resolve explicit executable paths against the invocation directory before either subprocess changes `cwd`. Preserve PATH lookup for bare executable names.
findings.title: Resolve relative `--node` paths before changing `cwd`.

findings.body:
**Accept `--json` and keep machine-mode stderr empty.**

`apps/crq-python/ops/deploy-controller.py:2010` builds the parser without a `--json` option. A call that passes `--json` fails argument parsing. The `_UsageError` path then prints the usage text to stderr and returns 2 before any operation runs. `apps/crq-python/test_deploy_controller_cli.py:273` and `:282` both invoke the controller with `--json`. Machine mode in `policy/DOCTRINE.md:14` requires stderr to stay empty, so this path breaks that contract.

The fix adds the flag, records machine mode before parsing, and gates the stderr narration in the error paths.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
@@ main() parser options
                              "before import, lock and preflight")
+    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true",
+                        help="machine mode: keep stderr empty")
     sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="operation", required=True)
@@
+    machine = "--json" in (sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
     operation = ""
     try:
@@ usage error path
         print(json.dumps(_error_artifact("usage", operation, str(exc), 2),
                          indent=2, sort_keys=True))
-        print("usage: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        if not machine:
+            print("usage: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
@@ operation error paths
     except RecoveryRequired as exc:
         print(json.dumps(exc.recovery, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
-        print("recovery required: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        if not machine:
+            print("recovery required: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
         return 3
     except NoChangeRefused as exc:
         print(json.dumps(exc.record, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
-        print("refused: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        if not machine:
+            print("refused: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
     except Refused as exc:
         print(json.dumps(_error_artifact("refused", args.operation, str(exc), 2),
                          indent=2, sort_keys=True))
-        print("refused: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        if not machine:
+            print("refused: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
@@ ValueError/OSError/CalledProcessError path
         print(json.dumps(_error_artifact("refused", args.operation, message, 2),
                          indent=2, sort_keys=True))
-        print("refused: " + message, file=sys.stderr)
+        if not machine:
+            print("refused: " + message, file=sys.stderr)
         return 2
```

</details>
findings.title: Accept `--json` and keep machine-mode stderr empty.
